This notebook writes `spack.yaml`. It should only answer:

> What scientific system dependencies does this project require?

Do not install the environment here, yet. Simply define the 
system dependencies that Spack can provide:

```{python}
#| sorting-hat: remove
from rse_workbench.sci_sysdeps import default_spack_env, write_spack_yaml
```


It can be useful to predict the system dependencies using
R's `pak::pkg_sysreqs()` function. If you need to customize the compiler
or any other configuration, do so in the dictionary below, and
the changes will reflect when you run `write_spack_yaml()`.

```{python}
#| sorting-hat: remove
spack_env = {
    "spack": {
        "specs": list(set(DEFAULT_SYSTEM_SPECS)),
        "view": "/work/.spack-env/view",
        "packages": {
            "all": {
                "compiler": ["gcc@11.5.0"]
            }
        },
        "config": {
            "install_tree": {"root": "/work/.spack-env/install"},
            "source_cache": "/work/.spack/cache/source",
            "misc_cache": "/work/.spack/cache/misc",
            "build_stage": ["/work/.spack/stage"],
            "shared_linking": {
                "type": "rpath",
                "missing_library_policy": "error",
            },
        },
    }
}

write_spack_yaml(project_contract.spack_yaml, spack_env)
project_contract.spack_yaml
```
